question.problem:
A robotic arm randomly selects a box in a warehouse containing $n$ items from $1$ to $150,$ with each value equally likely. The arm then randomly picks one of these $n$ items and scans its position number (from $1$ to $n,$ each value equally likely).

What is the expected position number scanned?

The expected position number scanned is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
This is a two-step random process: first, a box is selected containing $n$ items uniformly from $1$ through $150,$ and then an item is chosen uniformly in one of the positions numbered $1$ through $n.$

- Let $Y$ be the number of items in the box. Since this is an integer selected uniformly from $1$ to $150,$ we have $Y∼U\{1,2,…,150\}.$

- Let $X$ be the position number scanned, an integer selected uniformly from $1$ to $Y.$

We are asked to compute $\text{E}[X].$ Since the distribution of $X$ depends on $Y,$ we apply the tower property:

$$
\text{E}[X]=\text{E}[\text{E}[X∣Y]]
$$

Given $Y=n,$ the number $X$ is chosen uniformly from $1$ to $n.$ So, we have that

$$
\text{E}[X∣Y=n]=\frac{n+1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\text{E}[X]=\text{E}[\frac{Y+1}{2}].
$$

Now, we apply the linearity of expectation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \text{E}[Y+1] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (\text{E}[Y]+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Y$ is uniformly distributed on $\{1,2,…,150\},$ we use the formula for the mean of the first $n$ integers:

$$
\text{E}[Y]=\frac{150+1}{2}=75.5
$$

Substituting, we finally get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (\text{E}[Y]+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (75.5+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 76.5 \\  & =38.25.\end{aligned}
$$
